findings.label: Edited-post score not persisted
findings.description: _edited in watcher.py re-scores the post and fires a Telegram alert when the score shifts by ≥5, but never writes the new score, bucket, flags_json, or cv_variant back to the jobs row. A subsequent approve call rebuilds the match from the stale stored row.
findings.action: Add UPDATE jobs SET score=?, bucket=?, flags_json=?, cv_variant=? WHERE id=? after the alert fires in _edited, or introduce a pipeline.update_job_score() helper.

findings.label: Bot listener exits permanently on unexpected exception
findings.description: send_bot_command_updates handles a failed poll response with time.sleep(5)/continue but does not catch exceptions that escape the per-update try/continue block. An unexpected error from _bot_api or json.loads exits the thread; start_bot_listener logs 'bot listener crashed' once and never restarts.
findings.action: Wrap the while True body in an outer try/except Exception that logs and continues, or add restart logic in start_bot_listener.

findings.label: Subject-instruction lost for LLM-only extractions
findings.description: approve() re-extracts subject_instruction with regex_extract() only. An instruction the LLM extracted in a prose format the regex misses is absent at approval time because subject_instruction is not stored in the jobs table.
findings.action: Add a subject_instruction column to jobs populated at process_post time, or call the LLM at approval time when the regex finds nothing.

findings.label: _daily_count reports since restart, not today
findings.description: _daily_count increments on every processed post and never resets. The heartbeat says 'processed today: N' but N is the lifetime count since the watcher started.
findings.action: Track a (date, count) pair and reset when the date changes, or change the heartbeat label to 'processed this session'.

findings.label: approve() actor post-hoc correction is fragile
findings.description: _bot_approve and the agent's _t_decide both call approve() (which writes actor='user') and then correct it with a separate UPDATE. This works in the current single-threaded design but would silently mis-attribute concurrent approvals.
findings.action: Add an actor= parameter to pipeline.approve() so callers set it directly.
